newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Swire sets second perpetual.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Swire sets second perpetual.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd was back in the Asian debt markets on Wednesday with its second perpetual bond issue.
The bond was launched by Swire Pacific Capital and guaranteed on a subordinated basis by Swire Pacific Ltd, one of Hong Kong's blue chip companies.
For Swire, the perpetual bond issues represent a relatively cheap way of accessing funds. A perpetual bond never matures.

"With continuing increases in profitability and continuing increases in dividends, it doesn't take long before the perpetual bond becomes cheaper than equity," said Swire Pacific finance director Michael Bell.
The US$300 million note issue carries a coupon of 8.84 percent. It was launched and re-offered at par to yield 191 basis points over the U.S. Treasury bond due November 2026.
The notes can be called at par on the 20th anniversary and annually thereafter.
For Swire, this latest perpetual cost less than its first perpetual bond issued last October. That bond, which also was US$300 million in size, paid a coupon of 9.33 percent.
The earlier issue can be called after 10 years rather than after 20 years.
Bell said the company is unlikely to want to pay back the perpetual bonds "so whether there is a 10-year or 20-year call doesn't make much difference to us."

Bankers said they expected the geographical distribution of the bond to be similar to that of the last issue, where about 10 percent placed in Europe and the rest was roughly split between the U.S. and Asia.
Last week, Swire launched HK$3 billion in floating rate notes that traders said were very aggressively priced.
Proceeds of both issues will be used for general working capital, Bell said. "We've got various plans to spend bits and pieces here and there," he said.

Associates Corp of North America brought a US$500 million Euro-Asian floating rate note. The five-year FRN was priced at 99.837 to float at 6.25 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley were lead managers.

In other news, Thailand's Sinn Bualuang set a 6.0 billion yen FRN due in 2003. The notes, which have annaul puts and calls, pay a margin of 75 basis points over yen LIBOR and, with fees, an all-in return of 140 basis points.
